items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-23
items.q: I worked in that place two years, man. Me and Lee and Son Andy, Roy Evans, Joe Robeshow, and Plekton, Rennie Hall. That's all we had.

ctx.x: That's it. Rene Hall. That's who it was.
He opened up the place with us. Rene Hall.

items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-28
items.q: Rennie Hall. That's all we had. And the other people would come in and sit in, you know, sometimes.

ctx.x: He had Rene Hall, that's it, Rene Hall. He had Rene Hall, that's who it was.

Yeah, Rene Hall, that's who it was. He opened up the place with us, Rene Hall. Mm-hmm. You know, this band, and he brought that five-string band in there. Why are you a freak about, you know, banding and different things? That's what I call him Plectum. He'd let them get the way to the longer neck, you know, the rhythm. What are you experimenting on that? Well, you could play them, you could play with violin, too, you know.

items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-23
items.q: Me and Lee and Son Andy, Roy Evans, Joe Robeshow, and Plekton, Rennie Hall. That's all we had.

ctx.x: Why, that's it. Yeah, I did see one one time. I was looking for Rene, and I went to this Cadillac Club down on St. Claude, and they had one there, you know. But I never paid attention to it, you know. I'd rather listen to the music and find the girls later.

Man, them cats are taking, you buy a dollar worth of tickets over there, that day when you come in. The girls sitting all up there, now. With a dollar worth of it. Ten cents a dance. But the girls got a string of tickets about that long. You know. Mm-hmm. You start at the bottom, see. Boy, now they got a guy walk around. Mm-hmm. Take them tickets from you, you know. Mm-hmm. Girl got the tickets. She done snapped it off. Mm-hmm. Well, you get it this end. Band of the top, you know. Time for another snap-off…

items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-28
items.q: that was a bad consist of Roy Evans, Son Handy, Lee College, myself, Joe Rovershow. And that was all. No, Plectum. We called the guy Plectum. So that'd be one of the greatest band you'll play around here.

ctx.x: I mean, why he got off it, I don't know. Uh-huh. And, uh, that was a bad consist of Roy Evans, Son Handy, Lee College, myself, Joe Rovershow. And that was all. No, Plectum. We called the guy Plectum. So that'd be one of the greatest band you'll play around here. I'll do his name, and I'll see if I can think his name now. I call him Plectum, because he had one of them Plectum guitars. Five-string guitars. Banders, now. What is that little fella's name, man? He turned out to be one of the greatest, he's New York…
Yeah. Well, he had a couple of them, he had Rene Hall and he had Rene Hall. Rene Hall, that's it, that's it.
